title: deno-lock-osv.json — what of a deno.lock reached osv-scanner, and what could not
description: Emitted by bin/deno-lock-osv.mjs. osv-scanner cannot read deno.lock, so its npm packages are restated in osv-scanner's own input format and scanned from there. JSR and remote modules have no OSV ecosystem: they are listed here as unscanned and must never be read as clean. A record with error set and written null means the lane scanned NOTHING from deno.lock.

lockVersion.description: deno.lock `version` as read; null when the file could not be parsed that far.

npm.description: Distinct npm name@version pairs handed to osv-scanner.

jsr.description: JSR package@version keys present in the lock. Each is a dependency no advisory feed here covers.

jsrUnscanned.description: Always true: there is no JSR ecosystem in OSV. Stated so a reader cannot take the jsr list for a scanned set.

remote.description: https-imported modules in the lock, likewise unscanned.

written.description: Name of the osv-scanner input, relative to the converter's output directory, or null when nothing was handed over (no npm packages, or error).

error.description: Why the lock could not be converted. Non-null means the npm packages were NOT scanned.
